parts.title: Australia's democratic beliefs, rights and liberties
Government and the law in Australia

questions.q: Who are the traditional owners of the land in Australia?
options: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples
questions.explanation: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples are the first inhabitants, with oldest continuous cultures.

questions.q: Approximately what percentage of Australia's population are Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples?
questions.explanation: About 3% of population.

questions.q: When did the First Fleet arrive at Sydney Cove?
questions.explanation: First Fleet 11 ships led by Captain Arthur Phillip arrived 26 Jan 1788.

questions.q: How many ships were in the First Fleet?
questions.explanation: 11 ships.

What is jury service?

questions.q: What should you do if you see a crime or know someone is planning a serious crime?
options: Take the law into your own hands
questions.explanation: If people suspect someone may be planning a serious crime, they should report it to the authorities as soon as possible, to help keep the community safe.

questions.q: Which value: Australia's society values equality of opportunity for all, regardless of background?
options: True - equality and a fair go
questions.explanation: Core value: equality

questions.q: Is domestic and family violence against the law in Australia?
options: Yes, it is against the law and should be reported to police

Do people in Australia have to follow an Australian value of mutual respect and tolerance for others?
Is it acceptable to refuse to rent a house to someone because of their race?
options: No, discrimination based on race is against the law

questions.q: Should people in Australia make an effort to learn English?
options: Yes, English is national language important for participation

questions.q: What pledge do new citizens make?
options: Loyalty to Australia and its people, share democratic beliefs, respect rights and liberties, uphold and obey laws

questions.q: Is forced marriage allowed in Australia?
options: No, it is against the law

questions.q: What does freedom of religion include in Australia?
options: Freedom to follow any religion or no religion, but must obey law

questions.q: Does Australia allow freedom of speech to include inciting hatred against others?
options: No, freedom does not include inciting hatred

questions.q: What is expected about participation in Australian society?
options: Integrate, contribute, take responsibility, help when possible

questions.q: Is it important to support mateship and help others in times of crisis as in bushfire example?
options: Yes, Australians come together in times of crisis

questions.q: Who were the first people to live in Australia?
options: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples

questions.q: What is the Torres Strait?

questions.q: Australia is a constitutional monarchy. What does this mean?
options: King is Head of State whose powers limited by Constitution

questions.q: What is the role of Senate?
What is Australia's national gemstone?
questions.explanation: The opal is Australia's national gemstone. According to Aboriginal legend, a rainbow touched the earth and created the colours of the opal.

questions.q: What does the yellow circle on the Australian Aboriginal Flag represent?
questions.explanation: On the Aboriginal Flag, the black top half represents the Aboriginal peoples, the red bottom half represents the earth, and the yellow circle represents the sun.

questions.q: What is the white symbol in the centre of the Torres Strait Islander Flag?
questions.explanation: The white dancer's headdress is a symbol for all Torres Strait Islanders. The points of the white star represent the island groups.

questions.q: Which flags are officially recognised in Australia?
options: The Australian National Flag, the Australian Aboriginal Flag and the Torres Strait Islander Flag
The Union Jack and the Australian National Flag
questions.explanation: The Australian National Flag is the official flag of the nation. The Australian Aboriginal Flag and the Torres Strait Islander Flag are also officially recognised.

questions.q: In Australia's parliamentary democracy, where does the power of the government come from?
options: The Australian people, who vote for representatives in parliament
questions.explanation: The power of the government comes from the Australian people, because citizens vote for people to represent them in parliament.

questions.q: Can people in Australia protest against the government?
options: Yes, if the protest is peaceful and within the law
Yes, and they can damage property
questions.explanation: Australians can gather to protest, but protests must be peaceful and must not injure any person or damage property.

questions.q: Do men and women have equal rights in Australia?
options: Yes, men and women have equal rights
questions.explanation: Men and women have equal rights in Australia. It is against the law to discriminate against a person because of their gender.

questions.q: Under the Rule of Law, who must obey Australia's laws?
options: Everyone, including government, religious and business leaders and the police
questions.explanation: No person, group or religious rule is above the law. Everyone, including people in positions of power, must obey Australia's laws.

questions.q: If an Australian law and a religious practice conflict, which one must be followed?
questions.explanation: Where there is a conflict between an Australian law and a religious practice, Australian law prevails. Religious laws have no legal status in Australia.

questions.q: Which of these is a privilege of Australian citizenship?
questions.explanation: Australian citizens can apply for an Australian passport and re-enter Australia freely.

questions.q: Which of these is a responsibility of Australian citizens?
options: Serving on a jury if called to do so
questions.explanation: Citizens must obey the law, vote, defend Australia should the need arise, and serve on a jury if called to do so. Service in the Defence Force is voluntary.

questions.q: Who must vote in federal and state or territory elections?
options: Australian citizens aged 18 years or over
questions.explanation: Voting is a responsibility for Australian citizens aged 18 years or over, and it is compulsory.

questions.q: While overseas, what can Australian citizens ask for in times of need?
options: Consular help from an Australian government official
questions.explanation: Australian citizens can ask for help from an Australian embassy, high commission or consulate overseas. They must still obey the laws of that country.

questions.q: How do representatives in parliament answer to the people for their decisions?
options: They do not have to answer to anyone
questions.explanation: In a parliamentary democracy, representatives in parliament must answer to the people, through elections, for the decisions they make.

questions.q: Why does the Australian Constitution divide the power of government between Parliament, the Executive and the judges?
options: So the courts can make all the laws
To give the Prime Minister all the power
To stop one person or group from holding all the power
questions.explanation: The Constitution divides power between the legislative (Parliament), executive and judicial (judges) powers, to stop one person or one group from holding all the power.

questions.q: Who has the power to make and change laws in Australia?
questions.explanation: Legislative power is the power to make laws. Parliament has the power to make and change the laws in Australia.

questions.q: How many senators does each state elect?
questions.explanation: Each state elects 12 senators, and the ACT and Northern Territory elect two each, a total of 76 senators.

questions.q: After a federal election, who forms the Opposition?
options: The judges of the High Court
The party with the most members in the Senate
The party or coalition with the second largest number of members in the House of Representatives
questions.explanation: The party or coalition with the second largest number of members in the House of Representatives forms the Opposition. Its leader is the Leader of the Opposition.

questions.q: In Australia, can an employer refuse to hire someone because she is a woman?
options: No, this is discrimination and is against the law
Only if the boss prefers men
Yes, it is the employer's choice
questions.explanation: It is against the law to discriminate against a person because of their gender. A person should get a job based on their skills and experience.

questions.q: Is it acceptable to use violence to settle a disagreement with your neighbour?
options: No, violence is against the law
Only if no one sees it
questions.explanation: It is against the law to be violent towards another person. Australians believe in peaceful disagreement.

questions.q: Can a person in Australia be married to more than one person at the same time?
options: Only if their religion allows it
No, polygamy is against the law
questions.explanation: Polygamy (being married to more than one person at the same time) is against the law in Australia and can result in severe penalties, including prison.

questions.q: What does mutual respect and tolerance mean in Australia?
options: Only respecting people who agree with you
Only respecting people from your own culture
Listening to others and respecting their views, even when they are different from your own
questions.explanation: Mutual respect and tolerance means listening to others and respecting their views and opinions, even when they are different from your own.

questions.q: Do Australian laws apply to people from other cultures and backgrounds living in Australia?
options: No, they can follow the laws of their former country
Yes, Australian laws apply to all people in Australia
questions.explanation: Australian laws apply to all people in Australia. Regardless of your background or culture, you must follow Australian laws.

questions.q: In Australia, who can make their own choices about personal matters such as marriage and religion?
questions.explanation: Both men and women have the right to make their own independent choices about personal matters, such as marriage and religion.

questions.q: Is it acceptable to offer money to a police officer to avoid a fine?
options: No, even offering a bribe to a police officer is a crime
questions.explanation: In Australia, it is a serious crime to bribe the police. It is a crime to even offer a bribe to a police officer.
